faqs.question: Does the canister need to be agitated?
faqs.answer: It is recommended contractors shake the tank for 15-20 seconds before each use.

faqs.question: What equipment is needed to install AeroWeb?
faqs.answer: The AeroWeb system consists of three major parts: cylinder, hoses and gun. Guns are available with or without an ergonomic extension (useful for horizontal applications). All parts are sold separately. Use lithium grease or petroleum jelly on all fittings to prevent dried adhesive from clogging or seizing. Hoses and guns may be reused multiple times if maintained properly. The end of the gun should be cleaned with an appropriate solvent (i.e. acetone) at the end of each use and new grease or petroleum jelly applied. When changing to a new cylinder, close the valve and depressurize the hose. Remove the hose and attach it to a new cylinder. If the hose isn’t transferred to a new cylinder immediately, empty the hose and spray gun to ensure product does not harden in the hose and gun. When there is product in the cylinder, always keep the cylinder valve open to maintain pressure in the hose when not in use.

faqs.question: Are there temperature restrictions with AeroWeb?
faqs.answer: AeroWeb can be used in temperatures as low as 25°F. The tanks and material must be kept at 60°F or warmer. When applying in ambient temperatures below 60°F, store the cylinders in a heated space until ready to apply. The cylinders must be kept warm on the jobsite. Do not use cylinders for tarp weight when ambient temperatures drop below 60°F. When the material becomes too cold, it will begin to “spit” rather than spray from the gun. If this happens, switch it out for a warm cylinder.

faqs.question: What is needed to clean up and prep for next use?
faqs.answer: Use a safe solvent, mineral spirits or acetone depending on VOC regulations to clean tools and surfaces If the spray gun valve becomes stuck, attach the hose and spray gun to a cylinder of citrus cleaner or Low-VOC UN-TACK and trigger the gun until it operates smoothly. If the tip becomes clogged, use a small-gauge wire or torch clean-out tool after soaking the fitting in Low-VOC UN-TACK.

faqs.question: How are cylinders disposed when empty?
faqs.answer: The hose and gun are reusable. In most areas, the empty cylinder can be disposed as an aerosol can or recycled as scrap metal. Federal law forbids transportation if refilled.

faqs.question: Is AeroWeb low VOC?
faqs.answer: AeroWeb is compliant across all 50 states including California. Current California VOC compliance requires meeting less than 250 g/L VOC. AeroWeb is 206 g/L.

faqs.question: What is Detec TruGround Conductive Primer?
faqs.answer: Detec TruGround Conductive Primer is a patented water-based epoxy developed specifically for use in electronic testing of conventional roofing assemblies. Once applied to a non-conductive substrate, such as wood, insulation or coverboard, the primer enables electronic leak detection (ELD) testing of the membrane for the life of the roof. Detec TruGround Conductive Primer is placed on the substrate directly below the membrane. Any other conductive mediums placed below the coverboard will result in invalid leak detection tests.

faqs.question: What is ELD?
faqs.answer: ELD is a quality-control testing procedure designed to locate discontinuities in waterproofing and roofing membranes. ELD determines the location of the membrane discontinuities (breaches/seam voids) by applying an electrical current to the surface of the membrane. ELD can also be called: electronic water test, electronic breach detection, membrane integrity testing, membrane integrity survey, and electrical conductance testing. ELD can be low-voltage or high-voltage.

faqs.question: What is a leak detection system?
faqs.answer: “Leak detection system” can have different meanings depending on who you ask. A conductive medium below the membrane is often referred to as a “system.” The testing technology also can be referred to as a “system.” Mule-Hide Products considers a “system” to be an embedded, monitored product, distinguishing between control tests (such as IntegriScan), conductive mediums (such as Detec TruGround Conductive Primer), and fully monitored leak detection systems (such as PermaScan).

faqs.question: Can Detec TruGround Conductive Primer be used on buildings insured by Factory Mutual (FM)?
faqs.answer: Yes. Detec TruGround Conductive Primer is listed in more than 10,200 Mule-Hide Products RoofNav assemblies. RoofNav-listed assemblies are insurable by FM. Tests conducted by FM showed that the addition of a conductive medium between the membrane and substrate did not affect the performance of these roof systems, including adhesion and wind uplift. Details on approved roofing assemblies can be found at RoofNav.com. Additional options are available when the building is not insured by FM but a Mule-Hide Products system warranty is desired. Additional details are available by contacting the Mule-Hide Products Technical Service team or the local Mule-Hide Products Territory Manager.

faqs.question: How is Detec TruGround Conductive Primer applied?
faqs.answer: Detec TruGround Conductive Primer is applied using a brush or a 3/8-inch nap roller in a single-sided application. Gaps between substrate boards must first be filled to ensure electrical continuity. Detec TruGround Conductive Primer should be liberally applied with a brush to any gaps wider than 1/8-inch. For larger gaps, conductive tape is recommended. A thin coat of the primer should then be spread over the entire project area using a 3/8-inch nap roller. If the surface is black, the primer has been applied to an acceptable thickness.

faqs.question: At what temperature can Detec TruGround Conductive Primer be applied?
faqs.answer: Ambient temperatures must be 40°F and rising when applying Detec TruGround Conductive Primer.

faqs.question: Does Detec TruGround Conductive Primer need to dry before the membrane is installed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The primer should be completely dry before membrane attachment. It typically dries in less than 30 minutes, though longer drying times can be expected in cooler temperatures.

faqs.question: Does Helix look different than Helix Max?
faqs.answer: Helix is a greyish green. Helix Max is blue.

faqs.question: How cold can it be when using Helix?
faqs.answer: The substrate and ambient temperature must be above 32°F when using Helix. If temperatures are below 50°F, the adhesive must be kept above 70°F during application. Heated tank blankets (not band heaters) are recommended to keep the adhesive warm during application at 50°F or lower.

faqs.question: Can Splatter application be used for Insulation Attachment?
faqs.answer: Splatter application is not currently approved for attaching insulation with Helix. Splatter can be used to attach insulation with Helix Max (drums only, and special equipment required).

faqs.question: What is open time?
faqs.answer: Once adhesive has risen/foamed up, boards or Fleece Back membrane may be placed into the adhesive. Rise time may vary from 10-15 seconds on hot (100°F+) substrates to 5+ minutes on cold (32°F) substrates. d. Tack/open/working time of the adhesive may vary from 1 minute on hot (100°F+) substrates to 10+ minutes on cold (32°F) substrates.

faqs.question: Is the open time the same as with Helix Max?
faqs.answer: Open time varies between Helix and Helix Max. Reference applicable product data sheet for specifics regarding each product.

faqs.question: How much more expensive is it to attach insulation with Helix versus fasteners?
faqs.answer: As a general rule, material costs to use Helix is around 5 to 6 times more expensive than using screws when one layer of insulation is installed. Unlike mechanically fastening insulation where only the top layer is fastened, each individual layer must be adhered when using Helix. However, some of the major benefits to using Helix Low-Rise Adhesive can greatly decrease costs in other areas of the project, such as: • Reduced labor compared to standard fastening into concrete, gypsum, cementitious wood fiber (Tectum), and lightweight concrete roof decks

faqs.question: Can Helix be used to adhere to certain existing aged single-ply membranes like Helix Max?
faqs.answer: While Helix can be used to adhere to certain existing roof surfaces such as mineral/granulated mod bit cap sheets, or weathered smooth mod bit cap sheets, it cannot be used to adhere to existing Single-Ply membranes such as TPO or EPDM.

faqs.question: Who does adhesion tests?
faqs.answer: Adhesion tests are scheduled through your MuleHide Territory Manager.

faqs.question: Does Mule-Hide sell dispensing guns for Helix Low-Rise Dual Cartridges?
faqs.answer: No, dispensing guns may be purchased through ABC Catalog.

faqs.question: Are there restrictions for Insulation attachment?
faqs.answer: Yes. Insulation boards must be maximum 4’ x 4’ when adhesive is dispensed at 12” OC or when boards exceed 4” thickness. 4’x8’ insulation boards may be used when adhesive is installed at 4” or 6” on center up to 4” thickness. Heavier cover boards, such as DensDeck Prime and securock can be installed in 4’x8’ sheets with bead spacing up to 12” thickness.

faqs.question: Does Liqui-Flash need to be stirred or mixed before application?
faqs.answer: Liqui-Flash does not need to be mixed prior to application.

faqs.question: What kind of prep work is required before applying?
faqs.answer: The surface must be clean and sound. Product can be applied with brush or trowel. Some substrates may require primer so please reference the PDS for more information.

faqs.question: What is the shelf life of Liqui-Flash?
faqs.answer: 2 years. Store in a cool dry place. High temperatures and high humidity will shorten the shelf life.

faqs.question: What colors and sizes are available?
faqs.answer: 1 gallon pail and 3.5 gallon pail. White, Black, and Gray.

faqs.question: Can Liqui-Flash be reinforced with fabric?
faqs.answer: Fabric can be embedded in the surface to provide reinforcement and strength.

faqs.question: Can Liqui-Flash be used on single-ply membranes?
faqs.answer: New TPO membranes require the use of Mule-Hide Low VOC Primer and aged TPO membranes require the use of Si TPO Primer.

faqs.question: What is the application temperature of Liqui-Flash?
faqs.answer: 32 degrees F to 120 degrees F

faqs.question: Is Liqui-Flash self-leveling?
faqs.answer: Yes. It can be used to seal seams and make repairs on any slope. Viscous enough to avoid running and drain out issues.

faqs.question: Does Repair Hero need to be stirred or mixed before use?
faqs.answer: Repair Hero does not require stirring or mixing before use. Repair Hero does not skin over or separate in the can after opening.

faqs.question: Can Repair Hero be used on single-ply membranes?
faqs.answer: On EPDM membranes Repair Hero may cause some swelling.

faqs.question: Can Repair Hero be applied to wet surfaces?
faqs.answer: Repair Hero can be used on wet surfaces and under water. When applying over wet surfaces, additional pressure is required to displace water. Surfaces can be wet but they must be clean.

faqs.question: What is the shelf life of Repair Hero?
faqs.answer: Repair Hero has a two-year shelf life. However, if sealed and stored properly, Repair Hero can remain useable beyond two years.

faqs.question: What colors and sizes are available?
faqs.answer: Repair Hero is currently available in White, Black and Gray. Repair Hero is packaged in one- and three-gallon pails. The three-gallon pail is completely filled unlike some of the competition.

faqs.question: What kind of prep work is required before applying?
faqs.answer: The surface must be clean and sound. No primer is required. Apply with a trowel.

faqs.question: Does Repair Hero have temperature restrictions?
faqs.answer: Repair Hero may be applied in all weather conditions. In colder weather, Repair Hero should be kept warm before use.

faqs.question: Can Repair Hero be applied to Kynar®-coated metal?
faqs.answer: Repair Hero has excellent adhesion to Kynar-coated materials.

faqs.question: Can Repair Hero be reinforced with fabric?
faqs.answer: Repair Hero is a fibrated product, but fabric can be embedded in the surface to provide additional reinforcement.

faqs.question: Can Repair Hero be used on shingles?
faqs.answer: Yes, it adheres to asphalt shingles.

faqs.question: Is Repair Hero available in a tube?
faqs.answer: No, Repair Hero is only available in one- and three-gallon pails.

faqs.question: How many 4-packs can be stacked together?
faqs.answer: To reduce blocking, packs should only be stacked 4-packs up to five high. faqs.question: Is it necessary to prime the surface before installation?
faqs.answer: ShapeShift pitch pans require priming on certain surfaces to ensure proper adhesion of the pan itself. Refer to the ShapeShift product data sheet for more details.

faqs.question: Do I have to prime the inside surfaces of the pitch pan and projections before filling?
faqs.answer: Refer to the ShapeShift product data sheet for more details.

faqs.question: Is there an outside corner piece to make an “L” shaped pan?
faqs.answer: No, not at this time. Although it can be made in any size, the pans must be either a square or a rectangle.

faqs.question: What color is MP Liquid Sealant offered in?
faqs.answer: MP Liquid Sealant is available in White, Black or Gray in 2-liter foil pouches (4 pouches/per pail).

faqs.question: Can ShapeShift really install on a wall?
faqs.answer: Absolutely, and it is approved for use on MHP system warranties. When filled with JTS 1 sealant, ShapeShift pans provide an excellent way to flash those troublesome cables or conduits that penetrate parapet walls when a prefabricated pipe boot or split pipe boot will not work.

faqs.question: Are extra pieces available?
faqs.answer: Cartons are available in straights and corners. A carton of straights contains 16 pieces. A carton of corners contains 48 or 16 pieces.

faqs.question: Will unused product save until the next job?
faqs.answer: The threaded cap on the foil pouches allows any unused product to be saved for up to 30 days after opening.

faqs.answer: Fees vary depending on the type of warranty desired. Current Fees are listed on Mule-Hide Warranty Application forms.

faqs.question: Does the contractor need to provide material invoices along with Warranty Applications?
faqs.answer: Specific warranties may require submission of material invoices.

faqs.question: Does Mule-Hide require a total tear-off for Labor & Material Warranties?
faqs.answer: No, this is not required, but all areas of wet insulation must be replaced with new, dry, similar material, specific warranties may require an independent moisture scan of the roof.

faqs.question: Does Mule-Hide offer any pre-job “walk the roof” or job starts?
faqs.answer: Yes, Mule-Hide Territory Managers offer these services.

faqs.question: Can I use Mule-Hide Acrylic Water Base Bonding Adhesive to adhere flashings?
faqs.answer: Mule-Hide Bonding Adhesive (solvent based), Aquabase 120 (water based) or Low VOC Bonding Adhesive are used as a contact adhesive to adhere flashings to acceptable vertical surfaces.

faqs.question: What fasteners should be used for insulation attachment on a steel or wood deck?
faqs.answer: Drill Point Fasteners (#12) should be used with 3" Insulation Plates.

faqs.question: What is In-Seam Tape?
faqs.answer: In-Seam Tape is a cured, butyl based, two-sided adhesive tape that bonds on contact and is used to seam and eliminate applicator inconsistencies & voids. When applied properly (Mule-Hide Tape Primer must be used), it provides the fastest way to achieve strong, long lasting, watertight field seams.

faqs.question: What is Cured Cover Tape?
faqs.answer: Cured Cover Tape is a length of EPDM, factory-bonded to a cured butyl adhesive tape that is highly resistant to the most extreme weather & use situations. It is used to strip in gravel stops and drip aprons metal edging). When applied properly (Mule-Hide Tape Primer must be used), it provides a long lasting, high-performing seal. Cured Cover Tape is also used to strip in field seams, rows of seam plates or batten bars for membrane attachment.

faqs.question: What if I need to prove Mule-Hide EPDM meets a written specification or complies with a UL, FM or other code requirement?
faqs.answer: Just provide Mule-Hide with the following information: A copy of the specification Name & address to whom the letter should be addressed Your phone & fax number What is the UL/FM requirement? Deck type? Slope? Insulation type and thickness? Membrane and system? Building location and height? Overall dimensions? Parapet height?

faqs.question: Do I need walk pads for a large commercial roofing project?
faqs.answer: Walk pads are always recommended. Mule-Hide offers walk pads for each system/membrane type we sell.

faqs.question: What are the Warranty Fees for TPO Roofing Systems?
faqs.answer: Fees vary depending on the type of warranty desired. Current Fees are listed on Mule-Hide Warranty Application forms.

faqs.question: Do I need Walkway Rolls for a large commercial roofing project?
faqs.answer: Walkway Rolls are always recommended. Mule-Hide offers walk pads for each system/membrane type we sell.

faqs.question: Does Mule-Hide require a total tear-off for Labor & Material Warranties?
faqs.answer: No, this is not required, but all areas of wet insulation must be replaced with new, dry, similar material, specific warranties may require an independent moisture scan of the roof.

faqs.question: Does Mule-Hide offer any pre-job “walk the roof” or job starts?
faqs.answer: Yes, Mule-Hide Territory Managers offer these services.

faqs.question: What if I need to prove Mule-Hide TPO meets a written specification or complies with a UL, FM or other code requirement?
faqs.answer: Just provide Mule-Hide with the following information: A copy of the specification Name & address to whom the letter should be addressed Your phone & fax number What is the UL/FM requirement? Deck type? Slope? Insulation type and thickness? Membrane and system? Building location and height? Overall dimensions? Parapet height?

faqs.question: How many 4-packs can be stacked together?
faqs.answer: To reduce blocking, packs should only be stacked 4-packs up to five high. We have found that when stacked higher, the bottom rolls could crush a bit which could create blocking and a wavy sheet when installed. It is possible that the stacking issue can be heightened over the summer months due to the heat.

faqs.question: How many 4-packs can be stacked together?
faqs.answer: To reduce blocking, packs should only be stacked 4-packs up to five high. We have found that when stacked higher, the bottom rolls could crush a bit which could create blocking and a wavy sheet when installed. It is possible that the stacking issue can be heightened over the summer months due to the heat.

faqs.question: How many 4-packs can be stacked together?
faqs.answer: To reduce blocking, packs should only be stacked 4-packs up to five high. We have found that when stacked higher, the bottom rolls could crush a bit which could create blocking and a wavy sheet when installed. It is possible that the stacking issue can be heightened over the summer months due to the heat.

faqs.question: Do I need Walkway Rolls for a large commercial roofing project?
faqs.answer: Walkway Rolls are always recommended. MuleHide offers walk pads for each system/membrane type we sell.

faqs.question: Does MuleHide offer any pre-job "walk the roof" or job starts?
faqs.answer: Yes, MuleHide Territory Managers offer these services.

faqs.question: Does MuleHide require total tear-off for Labor & Material Warranties?
faqs.answer: No, this is not required, but all areas of wet insulation must be replaced with new, dry, similar material, specific warranties may require independent moisture scan of the roof.

faqs.question: What are the warranty fees for TPO Roofing Systems?
faqs.answer: Fees vary depending on the type of warranty desired. Current fees are listed on MuleHide Warranty Application forms.

faqs.question: What if I need to prove MuleHide TPO meets written specification or complies with a UL, FM or other code requirement?
faqs.answer: Just provide MuleHide with the following information: A copy of the specification Name & address to whom the letter should be addressed Your phone & fax number What is the UL/FM requirement? Deck type? Slope? Insulation type and thickness? Membrane and system? Building location and height? Overall Dimensions? Parapet Height?

faqs.question: Does this product comply with Utah VOC regulations?
faqs.answer: This product does not comply with the following Utah counties’ VOC regulations: Box Elder, Cache, Davis, Salt Lake, Tooele, Utah, and Weber. Low VOC Weathered Membrane Cleaner is available for use in these areas.

faqs.question: What membranes can this product be used with?
faqs.answer: Weathered Membrane Cleaner can only be used with EPDM and TPO membranes.

faqs.question: Does this product comply with California VOC regulations?
faqs.answer: This product does not comply with the following California counties’ VOC regulations: Alameda, Contra Costa, El Dorado, Los Angeles, Marin, Napa, Orange, Riverside, Sacramento, San Bernardino, San Diego, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano, Sonoma and Tehama. Low VOC Weathered Membrane Cleaner is available for use in these areas.
